vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moodle-connector
Version: 1.0.0

The moodle-connector skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed to interface with Moodle LMS platforms via REST API and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The documentation (SKILL.md) and configuration files (package.json, _meta.json) describe standard educational features such as course management, grade tracking, and file downloading. It employs security best practices like PBKDF2/Fernet encryption for credentials and uses well-known libraries (requests, cryptography, playwright). No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection were found in the provided files.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it says (Moodle API client, downloader and MCP server) but has inconsistencies between its runtime instructions and the registry metadata (undeclared required binaries/env, a package.json install hook, and instructions that fetch and run code from a GitHub repo) — review the upstream repository and code (especially the MCP server) before installing or running it with real credentials.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Moodle REST client, batch downloader, MCP server) align with the instructions: it uses Moodle tokens, browser automation (playwright) for login, and an MCP server for integration. Small mismatch: registry metadata lists no required binaries or env vars, but SKILL.md clearly requires Python 3.10+, pip, and optionally the MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD env var for headless operation. The included package.json with an install script that runs pip is unusual for a Python project but explainable.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits actions to cloning the GitHub repo, running pip to install listed requirements, running Python scripts, and optionally adding an MCP server entry to Claude's config. It asks the user to place a Moodle web service token into config.json and (optionally) set MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD. It does not instruct reading unrelated system files or exfiltrating data to unknown remote endpoints. However, the MCP server will run as a native tool if the user adds it to claude_desktop_config.json — that elevates the tool's ability to be invoked by the agent, so review mcp_server.py source before enabling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry (instruction-only skill). SKILL.md instructs git clone + pip install -r requirements.txt and playwright install, which are standard but will download packages and browser binaries from PyPI and Playwright releases. The package.json file contains an npm "install" script that calls pip and playwright; this is unusual but not necessarily malicious. Because installation requires pulling remote packages/binaries, users should inspect requirements.txt and the GitHub repo before running installation commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required env vars, but SKILL.md references MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD (used for encrypted credentials / headless operation) and requires the user-provided Moodle web_service_token in config.json. The skill will therefore rely on secrets supplied by the user (Moodle token and optional password); the registry should have declared these. The number and type of credentials requested are proportional to the stated purpose, but the mismatch between declared and actual requirements is a transparency issue that could trick less-technical users.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and no automatic install spec means the skill won't be force-included. The MCP integration requires a user edit to claude_desktop_config.json which, once done, exposes the agent to an MCP server process that can be invoked by the model—this is expected for MCP tools but worth reviewing. The skill does not request to modify other skills or system-wide settings on its own.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill generally matches its description, but there are several transparency problems you should address before installing or running it: 1) Inspect the repository at https://github.com/Jabir-Srj/moodle-connector (especially mcp_server.py, batch_downloader.py, and any code that handles credentials) to ensure there is no unexpected network exfiltration or logging of tokens. 2) Do not put real Moodle tokens into a tracked config.json; follow SKILL.md advice and keep config.json out of git. 3) Be aware installation runs pip install (will pull packages from PyPI) and Playwright (which downloads browser binaries); verify requirements.txt content. 4) The SKILL.md references MOODLE_CRED_PASSWORD but the registry metadata did not declare it — treat that env var as sensitive and set it only in secure contexts. 5) If you add the MCP server to your Claude/OpenCode config, the agent will be able to invoke the tool autonomously; only enable that if you trust the code. If you are unsure, ask the author for a signed release tarball or a short audit of the MCP server code before proceeding.
